recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not add the older proposed clinician-attempt wording unless Patient Care reopens the topic, because current wording is governed by later approved issues and already resolves the old unassessible ambiguity.
issue_request: FHIR-6868 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for the DSTU1 AllergyIntolerance criticality value "unassessible". It asked why the null-style value existed and whether it was time-bound or permanent; the resolution moved the value set into the C-CDA/V3 criticality terminology path and called for explanatory usage guidance.
initial_application: Historical source first moved the value set away from low/high/unassessible to V3 CRITL/CRITH/CRITU, with 4aafeeebac explicitly marking #6868 as updating the criticality value set to HL7 V3. FHIR-8646 later changed the visible FHIR code strings to low, high, and unable-to-assess.
additional_context: FHIR-8482 adopted the V3 CriticalityObservationValue family, FHIR-8646 superseded the visible code strings with FHIR-defined codes, and FHIR-12177 added later criticality-versus-severity guidance. FHIR-7715 is a duplicate of the same unassessible question. A separate FHIR-8646 commit from this reconciliation fixed the only stale active narrative row still showing CRITL/CRITH/CRITU.
reconciliation: No additional source change was made for FHIR-6868. Current AllergyIntolerance source uses low | high | unable-to-assess, defines unable-to-assess as inability to assess worst-case future-exposure risk, and treats missing criticality as unknown.
